message.content:
I don’t have live access to current air‑quality data, but you can quickly find the latest Air Quality Index (AQI) for Los Angeles from several reliable sources:

| Source | How to Check |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” and view the city’s current AQI and pollutant breakdown. |
| **AirVisual/AQI Forecast** | Go to https://www.iqair.com/usa/california/los-angeles or use the IQAir mobile app; it shows real‑time AQI, forecast, and health recommendations. |
| **Weather Apps** | Most weather apps (e.g., Weather Underground, AccuWeather, NOAA Weather Radar) display AQI values for major cities. |
| **Local News** | Many local news stations (e.g., ABC7, KTLA) report daily air‑quality conditions during their morning broadcasts. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, remember that an AQI of 0–50 is considered “Good,” 51–100 “Moderate,” 101–150 “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,” 151–200 “Unhealthy,” 201–300 “Very Unhealthy,” and 301+ “Hazardous.” For the most accurate and up‑to‑date information, check one of the links above.
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in Los Angeles. We need to provide an answer. There's no tool for real-time data. We can respond with general info or say we don't have real-time data. Probably mention typical sources like AQI. Provide guidance on how to check.
